title: Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems
main_claim: For a finite weakly reversible mass-action network with fixed positive rates, every positive stoichiometric class P has a compact convex forward-invariant set K_P ⊂ P that every positive trajectory in P enters in finite time. The entry time may depend on the starting point, but the set does not. This is the fixed-rate permanence conjecture, including unbounded classes.
sibling_notes: Family 149 sibling (Boundedness-and-persistence companion) reported no_gap_found on the same Lemma 2.1 / Cor 2.2 and cut-flux argument. This paper reproduces that lemma verbatim in substance. Its new ingredients are the strictness on P \ K_h (labels with slope in S^⊥ are inactive there), a uniform δ_h at each fixed scale, and the scale iteration K_h ⊂ int B_{√h}. All three check out. As the sibling noted, the argument would also cover rates that vary in time between fixed positive bounds, apart from the use of min k / Σk.
